article.story: DENVER -- — Forty years after his retirement from football and 48 hours after his death at age 75, the Denver Broncos set aside a game ball for Tom Jackson in the aftermath of their 38-24 win Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders. “I'd be remiss if we didn't start just by honoring Tom Jackson tonight,” Broncos coach Sean Payton said as he began his postgame news conference. “He got a game ball tonight, his family. He was part of the rich history, obviously. A tough loss for everyone.” Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored the “Orange Crush” and ESPN great following his death on Friday. Jackson's death was announced Sunday by longtime on-air partner Chris Berman, just as some of the Broncos' early risers were starting to arrive at Empower Field for top overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza's first career road start. For the coin flip, Broncos great Champ Bailey wore a No. 57 Jackson jersey following a moment of silence and a video tribute to the fiery cornerstone of the defense that led Denver to its first Super Bowl appearance in 1977. Linebacker Alex Singleton wore a bright orange Jackson jersey after the game, too. He said the team watched film of the old AFC West rivalry Friday and No. 57 showed up again and again on the highlight reels, which of course included the famous clip where he told John Madden, “It's all over, fat man!” as the Broncos began to tilt the balance of power in the Broncos-Raiders rivalry in the late 1970s. “Just what he means to the organization, what he means to the football world,” Singleton said, “he was a special guy and hopefully we did him justice today.” Indeed, Denver's defense sacked Mendoza five times, hit him another 10 times, broke up seven of his passes and intercepted him once — that came from nickel back Ja'Quan McMillian, who sealed the win with a 35-yard, one-handed pick-6 with 1:52 remaining and the Broncos (8-2) clinging to a seven-point lead. “We want the defense to be like that again,” Singleton said of the Jackson-led unit. “Orange Crush, stop-everybody defense, come to Mile High and get embarrassed.” Coleman scored on runs of 1, 4 and 7 yards, the latter two after the Raiders (4-7) had erased a 17-0 deficit. “It’s hard to play in this offense,” said tight end Evan Engram, who caught six passes for 74 yards Sunday. “It’s hard to be a rookie. I mean, I was in Year 9 last year in this offense (for the first time), and it was it was a grind for me to learn it.” The Broncos kept pace with Kansas City atop the AFC West by winning their sixth consecutive game since Payton took back the offensive play-calling duties. Mendoza finished 18 of 37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He was bothered not only by the pass rush but the crowd noise. “Those fans are crazy loud,” Mendoza said. “Played in some loud environments in my college days, but college is nothing like the NFL and they were very loud. And there was some helmet miscommunication as well, so that was another challenge that prevented itself, but just happy to work through those challenges and I think it was a great experience.” Bo Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards with one TD and an interception on a Hail Mary as the first half ended. “I think it should be like basketball where if you chuck it from half court it doesn't count,” Nix cracked. Las Vegas erased the final remnants of a 17-0 deficit when Mendoza hit tight end Ian Thomas for a 19-yard touchdown in the third quarter. The score came after Nix was stuffed by Maxx Crosby and Folorunso Fatukasi on a fourth-and-1 sneak from the Denver 39. “I don't regret the call,” Payton said. Coming off their bye week, the healthy Broncos had their most productive first half of the season, jumping out to a 17-0 lead. Denver's special teams blocked two of AJ Cole's punts, helping the Broncos win the field-position game. Ashton Jeanty, whose 46-yard run set up Matt Gay's chip-shot field goal, slipped past linebacker Que Robinson on a wheel route and reeled in Mendoza's deep pass for a 68-yard touchdown that cut Denver's lead to 17-10 at the half. Jeanty finished with 79 yards on 11 carries and added five receptions for 90 yards. Even though Mendoza has been sacked 11 times in two games — the same number of times Kirk Cousins was sacked in nine games before his deadline trade to Minnesota — Payton said he sees a potential Raiders resurgence led by Mendoza. “A much different Raiders team than we're used to seeing,” Payton said. Kubiak has an unhappy homecoming Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, whose father, Gary, led the Broncos to their last Super Bowl title, was asked if he could talk about his emotions of returning to Denver, where he also cut his teeth as a coach. “Yeah I could, I don’t want to,” he replied. “I wanted to win this game today and we didn’t win, and so we got to go win next week.” Injuries Raiders TE Brock Bowers was inactive with ankle and quadriceps injuries. DL Tim Keenan III (knee) and DT Adam Butler (concussion) left the game, and DT JJ Pegues appeared to injure his left shoulder in the waning minutes. Broncos DE Sai'vion Jones left with 1:37 remaining with an unspecified injury. Up next Raiders: Visit the Cleveland Browns next Sunday.
